A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSOFT research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained Appendices A–J against v3's extensions and new Appendices K–N.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments on language understanding, visual classification, mathematical QA, and commonsense reasoning, together with ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds rank-sensitivity results, weight-angle measurements, convergence curves, and memory/runtime profiling.

M1.justification: The SVD-based principal subspace, frozen projections and residual weights, Cayley/Neumann parameterization, and two trainable scaling vectors remain unchanged. Equations 6–8 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure; the new geometric discussion does not introduce an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six GLUE tasks, 19 VTAB-1K tasks, MetaMathQA-40K training with GSM-8K/MATH evaluation, and Commonsense-15K with eight reasoning benchmarks. New analyses reuse existing coverage or profile layer configurations, without adding a distinct data domain or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding main and constrained-budget comparisons retain their comparator membership, including SVFT in Tables 13 and 15. New diagnostic comparisons reuse previously evaluated GOFTv2, qGOFTv2, BOFT, and OFTv2; additional ranks and block sizes are configuration changes.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the diagnostic evaluation design: rank sweeps reach 512, angle inspection samples eight columns of the layer-6 query matrix, and Appendix M introduces separate forward/backward profiling of custom linear layers and Transformer blocks. It also adds H100 end-to-end memory tests and an RTX5090 CoLA rank sweep. The existing main benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the existing ablations, v3 expands rank sensitivity to CoLA and higher ranks, directly examines strict versus relaxed angle preservation in Figures 9–10, compares convergence trajectories in Figure 11, and tests memory/runtime behavior at layer, block, and model levels in Appendix M. These add substantial evidence about geometry preservation, optimization, and efficiency mechanisms.

E5.justification: Appendix M newly specifies averaging runtime over 100 forward/backward runs for the layer and block experiments. Both versions already report five-seed averages for GLUE and VTAB-1K; v3 does not establish increased training repetitions or add confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Headline benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial rank, angle, convergence, and profiling results. v2's Table 17 is retained and expanded as v3's Table 18: existing accuracies remain, ranks 2 and 512 and runtimes are added, and the rank-1 parameter count changes from 352 to 392. Table 17, Figures 9–11, and Tables 19–22 supply additional results under their stated settings.

T1.justification: The angle/norm preservation theorem and proof remain unchanged, and the Cayley proof changes notation only. v3 adds update-family dimensional reasoning in Section 4.1 and a block-diagonal/Stiefel formulation in Appendix L. Appendix E also revises GOFT's single-layer activation increment from 12bsh−8bs to 4bsh log h, with a corresponding Table 9 revision.

C1.justification: The abstract removes its higher-effective-rank emphasis, and Section 4.1 replaces the inference of potentially greater expressiveness than LoRA with an explicit statement that their update families are not directly comparable. The central PSOFT contributions and headline efficiency/performance claims remain.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly limits empirical evidence to models up to 8B and discusses larger-model sensitivity, backbone activation memory, and underfitting at small ranks. Expanded Appendices J–M add rank-selection guidance, interpretations of angular preservation, curvature/noise/generalization arguments, and explanations of profiling behavior. The main text also adds mechanisms attributed to DoRA's overhead and LoRA-XS's limitations.

D1.justification: v3 documents the additional profiling framework, PEFT version 0.17.0, hardware, input dimensions, attention-head count, and module placement, and supplies absolute training times for existing efficiency comparisons. Existing benchmark hyperparameter tables and the code-access URL remain unchanged; the new reproducibility statement mainly points to retained resources.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained after matching author and publication metadata updates. Sections 2 and 4.1 add more explicit positioning against DoRA and LoRA-XS and qualify the expressiveness comparison with LoRA, producing a limited substantive refinement of research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the expressiveness discussion, experimental interpretations, and rank guidance, while retaining most existing prose and section order. It inserts a scaling discussion before the conclusion, adds reproducibility, acknowledgment, and LLM-use statements, and updates affiliations and publication headers.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through paired angle heatmaps, a comparative loss-curve figure, a new CoLA rank table, and four profiling tables. The retained commonsense rank table gains rows and a runtime column, Figure 4's panels are rearranged side by side, and Figure 7's GOFT memory annotation is revised.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the geometry and efficiency arguments more directly assessable through the new diagnostics and profiling, while qualifying the LoRA comparison and explicitly discussing the 8B evaluation limit. These improve an already substantial empirical paper. The gains are tempered by overinterpretation: Appendix L's curvature/noise claims are not established by loss curves, and Appendix M's blanket single-layer memory advantage exceeds Table 19's evidence, where BOFT has a 1.8 GB forward peak versus 2.1 GB for several PSOFT configurations.
